summary: Theodorus Willem Juynboll (1866–1948) studied at Leiden University (~1884–1893) and held a post at Utrecht University in 1916. He taught Jan Gonda.
Theophil Gubler worked in linguistics and Indology. He earned his doctoral degree from the University of Basel by 1903, having studied under Jacob Wackernagel.
Thi Xinh Nguyen, a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, completed a PhD at Punjabi University under the supervision of Gurjit Singh Mann (attested 2013).
Thibaut d'Hubert is an Indologist who held posts at the University of Chicago and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026 as Vertretungsprofessor).

Thich Nhat Hanh (1926–2022) was a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy scholar. He studied at Saigon, Princeton, and Columbia universities, and taught at Columbia (1961, 1963–1964), Van Hanh University (~1964–1966), and Cornell (~1966).
Working in Buddhist studies, Thich Thien Nghiem earned a PhD from the University of Delhi under doctoral supervisor Shalini Singhal (attested 2012).
Thierry Mathou (born 1963) works in Tibetology. He studied at EDHEC Business School and Sciences Po, and served as an Associated Political Scientist at CNRS.

Thierry Meynard (born 1963), a scholar of sinology and philosophy, earned a PhD from Peking University under Yulie Lou (~1999–2003). He became Professor of Philosophy at Sun Yat-sen University (~2006) and director of The Beijing Center (2012).

Thinh Canh Quang, working in Buddhist studies and philosophy, completed a PhD at the University of the West (attested 2007) supervised by Kottegoda Warnasuriya, having also studied under Lewis Lancaster and Ananda Guruge.

Thinley Dorji Bhutia worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as Tibetan Teacher and Boarding Superintendent at Darjeeling Government High School, and served as Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and Chief Editor of Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 1994).

Thinley Norbu Rinpoche (1931–2011) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied at Mindrolling Monastery and under Dudjom Rinpoche (Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje). He founded the White Lotus School.

Thomas A. Forsthoefel, an Indology and religious studies scholar, earned degrees at Georgetown, Loyola University Chicago, and a PhD at the University of Chicago under Paul J. Griffiths. He became associate professor of religious studies at Mercyhurst University (attested 2007).

Thomas A. Tweed (born 1954) specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Stanford University (~1979–1984) under William R. Hutchison and served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (~1993–2008).

Thomas B. Ellis works in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania and was appointed Assistant Professor of Religion at Appalachian State University (attested 2009).

Thomas Blom Hansen (born 1958) is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar educated at Aalborg University. He held posts at the University of Natal, Edinburgh (~2000–2003), Yale (~2001–2003), Amsterdam (~2003–2011), and Stanford University (Professor of Anthropology, 2010).

Thomas Borchert, a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar, pursued doctoral research at the University of Chicago (attested 2005) and became Associate Professor of Religion at the University of Vermont (attested 2017).

Thomas Burrow (1909–1986), an Indologist and linguist, studied at Cambridge and SOAS. He served at the British Museum (1937–1944), SOAS (1938–1948), and as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford and fellow of Balliol College (1944–1976).

Thomas Christian Tychsen (1758–1834) studied at Kiel University (~1777–1779) and the University of Göttingen (~1779–1783). He spent his career at the University of Göttingen (~1784–1834), working in linguistics and history and archaeology.

Thomas Cleary (1949–2021) worked in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a Ph.D. from Harvard University, where he studied under E. Bruce Brooks, and a JD from the University of California, Berkeley.
Thomas Doctor works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling Monastery and the University of Lausanne under Tom Tillemans, and held a post at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.
